newsitem.title: USA: Astor Foundation to close next year.
newsitem.headline: Astor Foundation to close next year.

text.p: The Vincent Astor Foundation, which has donated more than $170 million to charitable causes in New York City, said Wednesday it will close down next year after almost 50 years of philanthropy.
The foundation, overseen by 94-year-old philanthropist Brooke Astor, announced it would distribute its remaining $25 million in assets in 1997, focusing on education.
Astor's husband Vincent, who died in 1959, established the foundation in 1948 for the "alleviation of human misery." Its grants have largely been confined to the New York City area.

Astor is perhaps best known for her support of the New York City Public Library. The foundation also has given money recently to Literacy Partners, projects by The Partnership for the Homeless, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public television and historic preservation.
Astor has been personally involved in the donations to nearly 3,000 institutions in the city and has made it a practice to visit them.
She said in an interview in Wednesday's New York Times that she has decided to spend more time travelling and writing poetry.
Vincent Astor, who was her third husband, built up his family's New York City real estate empire which started with John Jacob Astor in the early 19th century.
